content.Title: INTERMACS Profiles and Modifiers (excerpt)

Profiles.Description: Patient with life-threatening hypotension despite rapidly escalating inotropic support, critical organ hypoperfusion, often confirmed by worsening acidosis and/or lactate levels.

Patient with declining function despite i.v. inotropic support; may present with worsening renal function, nutritional depletion, inability to restore volume balance; includes patients unable to tolerate inotropic therapy.
Profiles.Time frame for intervention: Definitive intervention needed within few days.

Profiles.Description: Comfortable at rest and with activities of daily living but unable to engage in other activity, living predominantly within the house; comfortable at rest without congestive symptoms but may have refractory elevated volume status and often renal dysfunction; marginal nutrition/organ function increases risk.
Profiles.Urgency/Notes: Variable urgency; depends on maintenance of nutrition, organ function, and activity.

Profiles.Description: Patient without evidence of fluid overload, comfortable at rest and with activities of daily living and minor activities outside the home but fatigues after first few minutes of meaningful activity; may require measurement of peak oxygen consumption or hemodynamic monitoring to confirm severity.
Profiles.Urgency/Notes: Variable; depends upon maintenance of nutrition, organ function, and activity level.

Profiles.Profile: Profile 7. Advanced NYHA class III symptoms
Profiles.Description: Patient without current or recent episodes of unstable fluid balance, living comfortably with meaningful activity limited to mild physical exertion.
Profiles.Urgency/Notes: Heart transplantation or MCS may not be currently indicated.

Modifiers for profiles.Description: Can modify any profile; includes recurrent ventricular tachyarrhythmias that recently contributed substantially to clinical compromise, frequent ICD shocks or requirement for external defibrillation (usually more than twice weekly).

Frequent episodes requiring emergency visits or hospitalizations for diuretics, ultrafiltration, or temporary i.v. vasoactive therapy. Considered at least two emergency visits/admissions in past 3 months or three in past 6 months.

content.Notes: This extract focuses on profiles 1,2,5,6,7 and modifiers; device names and procedures are listed as modifiers but are not genes.
